summary.text: Deva Simmons, a retired educator with no party affiliation, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Florida's 18th Congressional District to Scott Franklin.
A Brooklyn native who has lived in Polk County since 2002, she describes more than two decades in education.

paragraphs.text: Simmons was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York, moved to Florida in 1995, and has lived in Polk County since 2002.
She graduated from Erasmus Hall High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Columbia College in 1990, and received a graduate degree from Adelphi University in 1995.
She has worked in education for more than two decades as a teacher, mentor, and advocate for students and families, and is listed as retired as of 2026.
Simmons has served on the board of the Boys & Girls Club of Lakeland and has volunteered with the AGB Museum of Art, kidsPACK, Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, and Polk County Schools.
Her campaign materials emphasized public education, teacher pay and affordability.
She received 3% of the vote to Scott Franklin's 50.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
